title: The Metadata API for SEO
description: Control your page’s title, description, and social share cards directly from React components.

slides.title: Why Metadata Matters 🔍
slides.content:
# SEO & Social Sharing

Search engines and social networks look for special `<meta>` tags in your HTML:

* `<title>` – tab title and search result title.
* `<meta name="description">` – snippet in search results.
* `<meta property="og:image">` – image when sharing on social media.

In plain React, you'd need a library like `react-helmet`. Next.js provides a built‑in Metadata API that works both statically and dynamically.

slides.title: Static Metadata (pages/about.js)
slides.content: Export a `metadata` object (or use `generateMetadata`) to set page‑level SEO.

quizData.question: Where do you define the static metadata for a page?

options.text: Inside the component with a `<meta>` tag
By exporting a `metadata` variable from the page file

quizData.explanation: Export a constant named `metadata` (or an async `generateMetadata` function) from any page or layout.

slides.title: Dynamic Metadata 🔄
Dynamic Metadata Example (pages/posts/[id].js)
slides.content: Generate SEO tags based on the actual post content.

quizData.question: What does `generateMetadata` allow you to do that static `metadata` doesn't?

options.text: Set metadata based on asynchronous data like a database query

quizData.explanation: `generateMetadata` is an async function that can fetch data and dynamically construct the metadata object per request.

slides.title: Template & Default Metadata 🗂️
Remember the Head Component 🧩
slides.content: If you're using the older Pages Router and not the Metadata API, you can still use the `<Head>` component from `next/head` to inject tags into the `<head>` of the document. The Metadata API is the newer, more declarative approach.
